lines.text: Next: how much should we trust one photo? We use sigma, the spread: how far off a photo might be.
For x and y, the code uses zero point zero zero five, plus zero point zero one times d squared, where d is the distance.
At one meter that's one point five centimeters. At two meters, four point five. At three, nine point five.
Why squared? Twice as far, the tag looks half as big, and depth comes from its size. So far errors grow fast.
For heading, the spread is zero point five degrees, plus one point five degrees per meter. Two degrees at one meter, three point five at two.
These are cautious first guesses, much bigger than our simulated camera's scatter. The team will tune them from robot logs.
The maths uses sigma squared, called the variance: four point five centimeters becomes zero point zero zero two zero two five. Our guess has one too.
